title: Trilateral Commission cross-network and biography-freshness pass, 2026-08-08
summary: Depth-2 audit of current Trilateral roster entries against authoritative employer, governance, and public-office sources, focused on cross-network bridges and independent membership-versus-biography freshness.

sources.title: Chevron Completes Acquisition of Hess Corporation
John B. Hess joins Chevron's Board of Directors
Peter Harder - Senate committee evidence, May 5 2026

evidence.observation: Laurence D. Fink is listed on the current Trilateral roster, while the World Economic Forum currently identifies Larry Fink as a co-chair and Board of Trustees member; this is a high-confidence cross-network bridge for identity resolution and exact relation modeling.

Jared Cohen is listed on the current Trilateral roster, while Goldman Sachs identifies him as President of Global Affairs and co-head of the Goldman Sachs Global Institute and explicitly lists his Trilateral, CFR, and CNAS affiliations.

The current Trilateral roster still describes John B. Hess as CEO of Hess Corporation, but Chevron completed its acquisition of Hess Corporation on 2025-07-18 and describes John Hess as former Hess Corporation CEO; he joined Chevron's board on 2025-07-29.
The current Trilateral roster describes Marek Belka as a Member of the European Parliament, but the European Parliament records his ninth-term service ending on 2024-07-15.

A current-government title on the Trilateral page is not automatically stale: Senate of Canada records show Peter Harder actively chairing a Senate committee on 2026-05-05. The Commission's rotate-off language therefore cannot be implemented as a naive rule rejecting every current public-office title.

gaps: The complete 484-profile archive still needs deterministic current-status reconciliation.
Cross-dataset identity aliases such as Laurence D. Fink versus Larry Fink are not yet normalized across all packets.
Current roster biographies should be refreshed field-by-field from authoritative employer or public-office sources before being treated as current role data.
The scope and exceptions of the Commission's rotate-off policy are not sufficiently defined to derive membership state from public-office titles alone.
caveats: Cross-network membership establishes an affiliation edge, not control, coordination, wrongdoing, or shared views.
Current inclusion on the Commission's roster is evidence of current roster status; biography text on that same page may still be stale.
Absence from a current roster is not evidence that a historical affiliation never existed.

workflow.next_action: Resolve current-roster identities to existing canonical dossiers, then separate membership-status timestamps from role/employer freshness timestamps.

notes: Roster-membership freshness and biography-role freshness are separate dimensions and must not share one current/stale flag.
The strongest immediate identity-resolution bridge is the Trilateral Laurence D. Fink record to the existing Larry Fink dossier and current WEF co-chair record.
Jared Cohen is a strong explicit multi-organization bridge because Goldman Sachs itself lists his Trilateral, CFR, and CNAS affiliations.
The rotate-off policy needs source-qualified interpretation rather than a hard-coded public-office exclusion rule.

classification_rules: Track current Commission roster status independently from current biography/employer-role freshness.
Use authoritative employer, regulator, legislature, or officeholder sources to refresh present-day role text.
Resolve exact identities before creating cross-dataset recurrence edges.
Treat explicit cross-membership as an affiliation only; do not infer coordination or misconduct.
Do not convert the Commission's rotate-off policy into a hard membership rule without source-defined scope and exceptions.
data.method: Checked selected high-signal current Trilateral roster entries against current authoritative employer, governance, and public-office sources; compared those results to queued cross-tie targets and existing dossier coverage; recorded confirming and countervailing examples.
data.narrative_role: cross-network bridge discovery, field freshness audit, and skeptic pass
data.research_question: Which high-confidence cross-network relations can be resolved from current Trilateral roster entries, and which current-roster biography fields are stale enough to require separate freshness semantics?

findings.finding: Membership-status freshness and biography-role freshness are independent dimensions.
findings.detail: John B. Hess and Marek Belka remain rendered on the current Trilateral roster with role text that authoritative current sources show is outdated. Current roster inclusion should not cause copied biography fields to be treated as current.

findings.finding: Laurence D. Fink is a high-confidence Trilateral-to-WEF bridge.
findings.detail: The current Trilateral roster lists Laurence D. Fink, and the current World Economic Forum governance page identifies Larry Fink as co-chair and a trustee. The repository also already contains a separate Larry Fink dossier, so identity resolution should precede duplicate entity creation.

findings.finding: Jared Cohen is a high-confidence Trilateral-to-Goldman/CFR/CNAS bridge.
findings.detail: Goldman Sachs currently identifies Cohen as President of Global Affairs and co-head of the Goldman Sachs Global Institute and explicitly states his Trilateral, CFR, and CNAS affiliations.

findings.finding: Current-roster role text contains confirmed stale fields.
findings.detail: The Trilateral page describes John Hess as Hess Corporation CEO despite Chevron's July 2025 acquisition and describes Marek Belka as an MEP despite his term ending July 15, 2024.

findings.finding: The Commission's rotate-off language cannot safely be encoded as a naive public-office exclusion rule.
findings.detail: The current roster includes public-office descriptions, and at least Peter Harder's Senate title is independently current in 2026. Policy scope or exceptions require direct clarification before use as a deterministic membership classifier.

findings.finding: The next implementation slice should resolve existing cross-tie targets into canonical identities and timestamped relations, not create duplicate person records.
